full_judgment: 2. The petitioner as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 59 of 1999 before the Court of Assistant Judge, 5th Court, Dhaka for declaration of title and subsequently, the said suit was transferred to the Court of Additional Assistant Judge, 2nd Court Dhaka and renumbered as Title Suit No. 143 of 1998. The plaintiff's case, in short, is that the suit property originally belonged to five brothers namely, Sheikh Abdul Kader, Sheikh Ameer, Sheikh Zamir, Sheikh Samir Uddin and Sheikh Ramiz Uddin, sons of Sukur Mahamud and was recorded in CS and SA Khatian. After their death the plaintiff purchased the suit land from all the legal heirs of the original landlords by registered sale deed No. 6946 dated 13-8-90, deed No. 373 dated 15-1-91 and deed No. 429 dated 17-1-91 and the plaintiffs are possessing the suit land peacefully. The plaintiff Nos. 1 and 2 became the owners by purchase and by inheritance. The defendants have tried to disturb the possession of the plaintiffs in the suit land by creating forged and fraudulent documents. As the plaintiffs are poor widows and they have no manpower and other power so they could not resist the defendants from mutating the case land in their name in RS Khatian by virtue of the said forged and fraudulent documents and could not take proper steps against the said mutation in time. The defendants have no right, title and possession in the suit land. The plaintiffs are in possession of the suit land by inheritance and by purchase. The defendants tried to take possession of the suit land on 5-1-94 and consequently the plaintiff filed the present suit. At the time of filing of the suit the valuation statement of the plaint has been given by the plaintiff at Taka 50,000 with a fixed court fee of Taka 30 only.
